resources.string: Same start and end as %1$d other rides. Today: %2$d min door to door · usual: %3$d min.
Stopped: %1$d min in %2$d stops (usual %3$d min, %4$d stops)
No single reason: a bit of everything.
Every Sunday at 20:00 you get this as a notification.
On my way home, I\'ll be there around %1$s (about %2$d min). — automatic message from RideScreen AA
On my way to work, I\'ll be there around %1$s (about %2$d min). — automatic message from RideScreen AA
📨 Tell someone when I set off…
When you tap this place while connected, they get a text with your arrival time.
Without SMS permission the messages app will open with the text ready to send.

Your passenger controls Android Auto from their own phone: they type the destination, move through the menus and change the music. The two phones talk directly over Bluetooth, without internet, and you only pair them once.
With the rider connected to the bike, tap Find and choose them. The first time, both screens will show the same code.
Visible as «%1$s». Ask your passenger to open Passenger mode on their phone and tap Find the bike.
When you connect to the bike, your phone becomes visible to your paired passengers (and only to them).
Forget %1$s? They will have to pair again.
Nothing goes through the internet. Only paired phones can connect, and they can only send destinations, Android Auto keys and music controls.
Looking for the bike… The rider must be connected to it (or pairing). Keep both phones close.
Passenger mode needs the Nearby devices (Bluetooth) and Location permissions to find the other phone.

Check that the other phone shows the same code:
%1$s
A short rising chime when the dash starts showing Android Auto and a falling one if the link is lost (it plays through your helmet if it\'s connected).
Opening and closing cards (title, map and summary)
«Made with RideScreen AA» on the closing card
If the speed or the map run ahead of or behind the picture, shift them here. It applies to every clip and the preview shows the result.
Couldn\'t download the street map (no connection?). Using the route line instead.
Videos you\'ve made of this trip

Android Auto on the phone got stuck: it took the connection but doesn\'t answer. Restart its head unit server (button below: ⋮ → Stop head unit server, then Start head unit server) and tap Connect again.
Another video is still being made; wait until it finishes.
A short vertical video for stories and reels with the liveliest bits: take-offs, bends, top speed and the arrival.
Delete this video from the gallery?
The song couldn\'t be mixed in, so the video was made without it. Please send me the log.

To fix bugs, the app sends anonymous error reports: a random id, the app version and the error text. No account, no routes, no Wi‑Fi passwords and nothing that identifies you or your bike.\n\nYou can turn them off now or anytime in Settings → Privacy.
Lets your chosen handlebar remote drive Android Auto on the dash.

Only reads the keys of the remote you chose in RideScreen AA → Controls, and only while Android Auto is on the dash. It does not read the screen, what you type or other apps. Other remotes, the bike and your intercom keep working as usual.

Pick a Bluetooth handlebar remote: while Android Auto is on the dash, its buttons move around Android Auto (+/− up/down, ‹/› left/right, centre = OK, hold = home, double = back) and never touch music or volume. Your intercom keeps controlling the music.
%1$s · needs the accessibility permission to work with the phone in your pocket.
No remote connected. Pair it in Android Bluetooth settings, press any of its buttons and try again. (Intercoms and headsets don’t appear here: they keep controlling music.)
For the remote to work with the phone locked, turn on «RideScreen AA · handlebar remote» in Accessibility. It only reads that remote’s keys while Android Auto is on the dash.

Connect on the dash's screen mirroring interface as usual (on the 125X, screen 3). Once Android Auto is on the dash you can switch to another interface to see the bike's original dash: the app stays connected and keeps logging the ride, and Android Auto keeps running in the background.

Go back to the screen mirroring interface and Android Auto is there straight away.

The dash only turns on its Wi‑Fi on that interface, so the first connection always has to be made there.
To reach the dash (its Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth), Android asks for «Nearby devices». The app doesn\'t use it for anything else.
The dash isn\'t asking for the picture: put it on its screen mirroring interface (screen 3 on the 125X) and tap Connect (if it still won\'t, switch the ignition off and on)
Waiting for the dash: put it on its screen mirroring interface
Remote with Key Mapper or Tasker

For a handlebar remote that only drives Android Auto (the intercom keeps the music): in Key Mapper (Play Store), turn on Expert mode with Shizuku so it works with the screen off, and map each button to the action Intent → Broadcast receiver with one of these names. RideScreen only obeys them while Android Auto is on the dash. Tasker and MacroDroid work too.

On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, RideScreen AA can only start by itself when the bike\'s Bluetooth connects if «Autostart» is on.\n\nTurn it on for RideScreen AA on the next screen. While you\'re there, set battery saver to «No restrictions».
If the dash shows 00:00 or a wrong time, the app drops the link for a few seconds and reconnects so the dash takes the phone\'s time again. Android Auto keeps running.
Allow «Nearby devices» (Wi‑Fi) so the app can reach this dash over Wi‑Fi Direct
Android 17: allow «Nearby devices» so the app can talk to the dash on its Wi‑Fi

To read the battery over Bluetooth, type your bike\'s PKE code. You\'ll find it in the official Zontes Smart app → vehicle management, under the bike. This only reads the battery: it never locks, unlocks or changes anything on the bike (that\'s a separate, confirmed-each-time action in Help → 🔒 Lock / unlock).
Reading the keyless box over Bluetooth… the bike must be nearby.
⚠️ Low — if the bike has been parked a while, it may need a run or a charge.
Allow «Nearby devices» so the app can reach the keyless box over Bluetooth, then try again.
Bluetooth is off — turn it on and try again.
Couldn\'t find the keyless box. Get closer to the bike, make sure the official app isn\'t connected to it, and try again.
The box answered but didn\'t report the voltage. Please send me the log.
Set your PKE code first, in Help → 🔋 Battery (keyless box).

Needed once, only for locking/unlocking/releases. It isn\'t on the bike\'s QR code and isn\'t readable over Bluetooth: the official Zontes Smart app fetches it from Zontes\' own servers after login and keeps it on your phone. You\'ll need to get it from a phone where that app is already set up on your bike.
Enter the McuID (hex, at least 4 characters)
This sends a real command to the bike over Bluetooth right now. The bike must be nearby and the official app must not be connected to it.
Sending the command over Bluetooth… the bike must be nearby.
Command sent. Check the bike to confirm it worked — this feature hasn\'t been validated against hardware yet, please send me the log either way.
The box didn\'t answer the handshake, so nothing was sent. Get closer to the bike, make sure the official app isn\'t connected to it, and try again.
The box answered but its handshake couldn\'t be read, so nothing was sent. Please send me the log.
The device key (McuID) looks wrong: it must be hexadecimal and the right length. Nothing was sent. Check it and enter it again.
Couldn\'t build the command from the handshake, so nothing was sent. Please send me the log.
